identity.name: PENNAR INDUSTRIES LTD
identity.industry: Pre-Engineered Buildings, Industrial Steel Structures & Process Equipment

summary.oneLiner: Pennar delivered record FY26 revenue (INR 3,666 cr) and PAT (INR 139 cr) driven by US data center demand and a strategic mix shift to high-margin businesses, resolving prior labor bottlenecks to target 20% PAT growth in FY27. The key inflection is the scaling of US subsidiaries and boiler orders which are expanding margins despite rising working capital needs.

one-line thesis: Pennar delivered record FY26 revenue (INR 3,666 cr) and PAT (INR 139 cr) driven by US data center demand and a strategic mix shift to high-margin businesses, resolving prior labor bottlenecks to target 20% PAT growth in FY27. The key inflection is the scaling of US subsidiaries and boiler orders which are expanding margins despite rising working capital needs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 934 cr (Q4), INR 3,666 cr (FY26, +12.3% YoY); EBITDA: INR 114 cr (Q4), INR 401 cr (FY26, ~11% margin); PAT: INR 41 cr (Q4, +14.9% YoY), INR 139 cr (FY26, +16.2% YoY); Order Book: INR 810 cr (PEB India), $63m (PEB US), INR 145 cr (Boilers); Net Debt: Gross debt rose due to Telco acquisition and WC, but cash at INR 206 cr; One-offs: Forex gains boosted other income; higher inventory build-up for price hedging.
guidance: PAT growth of 20% for FY27; Revenue double-digit growth expected; Margins to expand sequentially as high-margin mix (US, Engg Services) increases; Capex ~INR 100 cr focused on automation and BIW completion.
order book & pipeline: Total visible backlog robust: PEB India INR 810 cr (tactical rejection of low-margin INR 150 cr order noted); PEB US $63m (includes Ascent); Boilers INR 145 cr (record high with 100 TPH AFBC); Hydraulics INR 34 cr.
segment / subsidiary detail: PEB India: Capacity utilization 70%, labor issues resolved, backlog growing. PEB US: Double-digit growth, anchored by data centers/warehouses, scaling Ascent/Telco. Engineering Services: AI-assisted design driving efficiency, outperforming. Boilers: Major growth lever with large order wins. Hydraulics: Stabilizing post-tariff impact, exploring Europe.
growth verticals / optionality: US data center capex cycle; Boiler segment entering high-growth phase with large capacity orders; Engineering Services scaling via AI automation and US/Europe expansion; Automation reducing long-term labor cost arbitrage risks.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 PAT margin 4.44% (up from 3.9%); FY26 PAT margin 3.83%. Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation passed through to customers. Labor costs rising in India/US mitigated by automation (robotic welding, AI design). Targeting sustained margin expansion via mix shift.
capex / expansion: FY27 capex guidance <INR 100 cr. Key spends: Completion of BIW Hyundai plant (2-3 months), robotic welding lines in US, automation in painting/assembly in India to counter labor scarcity.
capital allocation: Disciplined deployment into high-ROCE businesses (PEB US, Boilers). Working capital optimization target: reduce days from 82 to 75. Debt-equity target <0.8x by FY27 end (currently ~0.98x gross, lower net of cash).
risks & watch-items: Working capital bloating (debtor/inventory days up); Labor availability in India requiring costly automation; Raw material price volatility; Execution risk on large boiler orders; US tariff/policy changes.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; Emphasizes 'right to win' in specific segments; Transparent on labor/capex challenges; Committed to 20% PAT growth despite macro noise.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly rejected a INR 150 cr order to protect product mix/margins, signaling a shift from top-line chasing to quality growth. AI is framed as a margin-accretive tool for design detailing rather than a disruption threat.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.
